item.title: RKS U17 focuses on discipline ahead of Deans final
Lelean U19 back to the drawing board in bid to restore Deans glory
item.description: It is back to the drawing board for the Lelean Memorial School Under 19 side as they look to restore their former glory heading into this weekend’s Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans final. Under 19 Coach Peni Vakatawakoula highlighted this following their 36-27 semi-final victory over Ratu Navula College in Lautoka.
item.content:encoded:
It is back to the drawing board for the Lelean Memorial School Under 19 side as they look to restore their former glory heading into this weekend’s Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans final.

Under 19 Coach Peni Vakatawakoula highlighted this following their 36-27 semi-final victory over Ratu Navula College in Lautoka.

Vakatawakoula says they are looking forward to the final this weekend, adding that playing on the big stage is nothing new to the side.

He says heading into the semi-final, they knew they had to be tough and tighten up their defence and attacking patterns.

Vakatawakoula says these are areas they will continue to work on this week as they prepare to face Navatu Secondary School, who have made history as the first team from the Northern Division to reach a Deans final.

He says they firstly want to thank the Lord for giving them the strength, power and knowledge to secure the victory against a quality Ratu Navula side.

The coach says the players also wore black armbands in memory of Lelean old scholar Saimoni Vunilagi, who recently passed away in Japan, and extended their deepest condolences to his family.

Lelean Memorial School will face Navatu Secondary in the Under 19 final, with the time yet to be confirmed.

In the Under 18 final, Lelean will take on Suva Grammar School.

item.title: Kikau hopeful Kamikamica can recover in time for Rugby League World Cup
item.description: Fiji Bati forward Viliame Kikau remains hopeful that captain Tui Kamikamica will recover in time to lead Fiji at the 2026 Rugby League World Cup, while Caleb Navale is also expected to feature after making a remarkable return from an ACL injury. item.content:encoded:
Fiji Bati forward Viliame Kikau remains hopeful that captain Tui Kamikamica will recover in time to lead Fiji at the 2026 Rugby League World Cup, while Caleb Navale is also expected to feature after making a remarkable return from an ACL injury.

Kamikamica has not played since the Melbourne Storm's Round 4 NRL match against the North Queensland Cowboys on March 28 , after suffering a stroke that temporarily left him unable to speak or move.

The 32-year-old underwent brain and heart surgery and has since made a strong recovery.

He is currently touring the Papua New Guinea Highlands with former Storm team-mate and Kumuls great Justin Olam.

Kamikamica had initially hoped to return midway through the season, but a setback has prevented him from playing a match this year.

Despite this, the Fijian prop remains hopeful of making the Bati squad for the World Cup.

Navale is also set to return after making his comeback for Manly in their 18–12 NSW Cup loss to the Warriors on Saturday.

The second-rower returned just six months and three days after rupturing his ACL at pre-season training on 11 February, with his recovery reportedly believed to be the quickest in NRL history.

Kikau says Bati players are hoping to have the opportunity to play alongside Kamikamica in Fiji's World Cup matches against the Cook Islands in Newcastle on 18 October, Australia in Townsville on 25 October and New Zealand on the Gold Coast on 31 October.

Kamikamica has played 23 Tests for Fiji and 142 NRL matches for the Storm.

item.title: Labasa thrash Tailevu/Naitasiri 7-1 in Extra Premier League
item.description: Labasa FC have produced a dominant performance to thrash Tailevu/Naitasiri FC 7-1 in their 2026 Extra Premier League clash at the HFC Bank Stadium this afternoon. The Babasiga Lions took control of the match in the first half, scoring four goals to take a commanding 4-1 lead into the break.
item.content:encoded:
Labasa FC have produced a dominant performance to thrash Tailevu/Naitasiri FC 7-1 in their 2026 Extra Premier League clash at the HFC Bank Stadium this afternoon.

The Babasiga Lions took control of the match in the first half, scoring four goals to take a commanding 4-1 lead into the break.

Labasa continued to dominate in the second half, adding another three goals while keeping Tailevu/Naitasiri scoreless to seal the emphatic victory.

The 7-1 result gives Labasa another important win in their 2026 Extra Premier League campaign.

They have secured another crucial three points.

In other matches, Suva thrashed Nadroga 7-0, Navua beat Nasinu 2-1, while Lautoka edged Nadi 2-1.

item.title: Springboks admit Fijiana forced them to adapt in hard-fought Lautoka Test
item.description: The Vodafone Fijiana XV may have fallen short of victory, but their vastly improved performance against the Springbok Women has earned praise from the South African coaching staff, who admit Fiji forced them to adapt and adjust their game plan. Springbok Women assistant coach Franzel September says they expected Fijiana to come back stronger in the second Test after South Africa comfortably won th
item.content:encoded:
The Vodafone Fijiana XV may have fallen short of victory, but their vastly improved performance against the Springbok Women has earned praise from the South African coaching staff, who admit Fiji forced them to adapt and adjust their game plan.

Springbok Women assistant coach Franzel September says they expected Fijiana to come back stronger in the second Test after South Africa comfortably won the opening match 55-12, and Fiji did exactly that.

September described the 29-22 victory at Churchill Park in Lautoka as a proper Test match.

Fijiana made a strong start and took a 10-5 lead into half-time, while they led South Africa twice during the match.

September says the conditions were not easy, and the fired-up Fijiana side added to the challenge for the visitors.

He says Fiji's offloading game was particularly effective and tested South Africa in different areas, forcing his side to adapt and adjust their strategies during the match.

Despite the pressure from Fijiana, South Africa fought back in the second half, with debutant wing Maria Tshiremba scoring three tries to help secure the seven-point victory.

September says the coaches were pleased with Tshiremba's performance after backing her with selection for the match.

The victory completed a 2-0 series sweep for the Springbok Women and secured the inaugural Ubuntu–Bula Trophy.

The Springbok Women will face New Zealand's Black Ferns in Johannesburg early next month.

The South African squad will return home on Monday evening.

item.title: All Blacks ready to raise the intensity as Springboks showdown looms
item.description: The All Blacks have wrapped up their preparations for their first Test against the Springboks with an impressive 50-19 win over the Vodacom Bulls, but coach Dave Rennie says they will need to lift their intensity when they face the world champions in Johannesburg next Sunday. The All Blacks ran in eight tries against the Bulls at Loftus Versfeld in Pretoria to complete the opening phase of their S
item.content:encoded:
The All Blacks have wrapped up their preparations for their first Test against the Springboks with an impressive 50-19 win over the Vodacom Bulls, but coach Dave Rennie says they will need to lift their intensity when they face the world champions in Johannesburg next Sunday.

The All Blacks ran in eight tries against the Bulls at Loftus Versfeld in Pretoria to complete the opening phase of their South African tour with three wins from three.

Rennie says there were plenty of positives from the performance, particularly at set piece, with the All Blacks making significant progress in their scrum following their 38-21 win over the Stormers in their opening tour match.

He says the side created plenty of opportunities against the Bulls, making 11-line breaks to one, although he believes they still left some points on the field.

All Blacks captain Codie Taylor says the Bulls tested them at times, but the team knows the physicality and intensity will rise significantly when they meet the Springboks.

Taylor says the forward pack has made good progress during the tour but admits they are still not the finished product.

The three warm-up matches against the Stormers, Sharks and Bulls have also given the All Blacks valuable exposure to South African rugby ahead of the four-Test series against their traditional rivals.

Attention now turns to the fitness of Damian McKenzie, Cam Roigard and Will Jordan ahead of the first Test.

Rennie says Roigard and Jordan are expected to be available, while there is more uncertainty around McKenzie as he continues his recovery from an ankle injury.

Meanwhile, Richie Mo'unga has arrived in South Africa after earning his first All Blacks call-up since the 2023 Rugby World Cup final.

However, Rennie has confirmed Mo'unga will not be considered for the first Test against the Springboks as he needs time to familiarise himself with the team's systems after spending three years playing in Japan.

Mo'unga could instead make his return to the All Blacks against the Lions four days after the opening Test.

The All Blacks will take on the Springboks next Saturday at 3am.

item.title: Rewa FC to face Auckland City in OFC Men’s Champions League semi-final
item.description: Rewa FC will take on defending champions Auckland City FC in the OFC Men’s Champions League semi-final on Wednesday at 4R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba. This is after Auckland came from behind in the final minutes of added time to complete a dramatic 4–3 comeback against Tahiti’s AS Venus.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC will take on defending champions Auckland City FC in the OFC Men’s Champions League semi-final on Wednesday at 4R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba.

This is after Auckland came from behind in the final minutes of added time to complete a dramatic 4–3 comeback against Tahiti’s AS Venus.

The Delta Tigers secured their place in the knockout stage after defeating Papua New Guinea’s Lae City FC 2–1 in their must-win final Group B match yesterday.

Merrill Nand and Kavaia Rawaqa scored for Rewa as they secured the crucial victory needed to progress.

Rewa had a difficult start to the tournament, losing 4–1 to Vanuatu’s Galaxy FC in their opening match.

They bounced back strongly with a 4–2 victory over Tupapa Maraerenga before beating Lae City 2–1 to book their place in the semi-finals.

Rewa will now turn their attention to Auckland City as they look to secure a place in the OFC Men’s Champions League final.

The semi-finals will be played on Wednesday at 4R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba, with matches scheduled for 3pm and 7pm.

The final will be played at the same venue at 3pm on Saturday.

item.title: All Blacks make it three from three with dominant 50-19 win over Bulls
item.description: The emphatic win at Loftus Versfeld also saw loose forward Anton Segner emerge as a star in the making , with the 25-year-old delivering an outstanding performance. The openside flanker, who made his Test debut last month, was named man of the match after impressing with his pace, strength, defensive ability and work rate .
item.content:encoded:
The emphatic win at Loftus Versfeld also saw loose forward Anton Segner emerge as a star in the making , with the 25-year-old delivering an outstanding performance.

The openside flanker, who made his Test debut last month, was named man of the match after impressing with his pace, strength, defensive ability and work rate .

Segner could now push Luke Jacobson for a place in the match-day squad when the All Blacks face the Springboks in their first Test in Johannesburg next week.

Centre Rieko Ioane was another standout performer as the All Blacks ran in eight tries to three against a Bulls side that played with plenty of adventure and skill, particularly in the second half.

Ioane looked re-energised on his return to the side following his sabbatical, with his form coming at a crucial time after Billy Proctor returned to New Zealand with a fractured shoulder blade.

The All Blacks also showed significant improvement at scrum time, with props Xavier Numia and Tyrel Lomax making a strong impact, supported by locks Fabian Holland and Patrick Tuipulotu.

Holland continued his impressive tour with another lively performance, including an excellent offload that put captain Codie Taylor over for his second try.

He also made his presence felt at the breakdown, an area where the All Blacks applied considerable pressure on the Bulls.

Their maul defence was also much improved, with the visitors shutting down several Bulls attacks close to their try line.

The All Blacks conceded just eight penalties, showing better discipline than in their earlier wins over the Stormers and Sharks.

The Bulls, meanwhile, were reduced to 14 men after prop Francois Klopper was sin-binned for a cynical offside after 30 minutes.

The All Blacks were generally clinical inside the Bulls' 22, although some of their finishing when attacking from deep left room for improvement.

Head coach Dave Rennie said afterwards that his side's performance was "mixed".

He said the All Blacks also needed to improve their offloading, particularly in the wet conditions.

Rennie also provided an update on the fitness of backs Cam Roigard and Will Jordan, who have yet to feature on tour, saying he was confident both would be available for the first Test.

Damian McKenzie, however, remains a greater concern after suffering an ankle sprain against the Sharks, although Rennie said he was confident the fullback would recover.

Taylor's return from a calf injury will also please the All Blacks coach, with the captain playing 40 minutes and scoring two tries.

Josh Moorby and Leroy Carter also scored two tries each, while Ioane and replacement loose forward Wallace Sititi were the other try scorers.

The All Blacks now turn their attention to the Springboks, whom they will face next Sunday at 3am.
